headline: Long-read and single-cell assays now resolve methylation and histone marks by cell type
label: Cell Type Resolved Regulatory Profiling
summary: Bulk long-read and single-cell assays now attribute methylation and histone-mark states to individual cell types.
synthesis: The common thread is attributing epigenomic regulatory state to specific cells. COMET assigns individual long reads to cell types using cell-type-specific methylation, enabling cell-type-resolved analysis from bulk long-read data across human tissues, and LongReadClock applies the same logic to build cell-type-resolved epigenetic aging clocks from bulk blood. TrES-seq jointly profiles scRNA-seq with H3K27ac, H3K27me3 and H3K9me3 through nanobody-Tn5 fusions, linking histone marks to transcriptional axes of cell identity. FiberTron is trained on a single Fiber-seq/Nanopore sample to predict base-resolution methylation and accessibility. What is new is the direct coupling of epigenomic readouts to cell identity. The remaining items, on somatic haplotyping, donor-specific assemblies, long-read RNA-seq diagnostics and sample mispairing, address adjacent genomics questions rather than cell-type attribution.
